metadata.source_policy: Links checked for core event and timing only; source independence and image rights stored separately.
metadata.note: 18 core-identity case reviews; Jan 28 Montana giant-snowflake lead held due to source/date disagreement; not fact-checked or publication-ready.

cases.title: The Great Blizzard of 1978 reaches Ohio and the Great Lakes
cases.primary_angle: Explain how explosive cyclone deepening and Arctic air created near-total transport paralysis.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare observed pressure and winds with 1978 warning bulletins; distinguish land observations from the storm central pressure.
cases.verified_core_fact: On January 26, 1978 a rapidly deepening storm brought destructive blizzard conditions to Ohio and surrounding Great Lakes states.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: U.S. NWS storm maps, archived surface analyses and original warning texts; use specific observation locations and timestamps.
cases.research_note: Duration Jan 25–27; no single-day totals as full-storm totals; NWS studies within NOAA are not institutionally independent.

cases.title: The mysterious 1884 Enigma tornado outbreak
cases.primary_angle: Why a devastating 1884 outbreak remains difficult to reconstruct despite early attempts at tornado forecasting.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how John Park Finley's contemporary observations shaped early tornado forecasting without claiming a precise modern outbreak count.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Enigma tornado outbreak began February 19, 1884, affecting the U.S. Southeast; historical documentation cannot conclusively establish the number of tornadoes.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NOAA Heritage includes a specific Finley historical tornado map credited Public Domain; do not imply exact modern tracks.
cases.research_note: Both sources within NOAA/NWS; 19–20 Feb outbreak, counts disputed. NOAA Heritage specifically labels the Finley map public domain, not necessarily other assets.

cases.title: Gainesville's catastrophic 1936 tornado
cases.source_publisher: Digital Library of Georgia / Georgia Archives
cases.primary_angle: Use original documented Gainesville streetscape damage rather than an uncertain single tornado-path reconstruction.
cases.alternate_angle: Explore visibility and urban vulnerability using dated photographs; do not conflate Tupelo's April 5 toll with Gainesville's April 6 toll.
cases.verified_core_fact: A destructive tornado struck Gainesville, Georgia on April 6, 1936, documented in contemporary Georgia archival photography.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Georgia Archives original dated photographs and city streets; individual photograph licensing must be checked.
cases.research_note: NWS biographical page gives potentially inaccurate specific school casualty figures; do NOT reuse those statistics. Verify individual photo rights with Georgia Archives.

cases.title: The deadly 1953 Waco downtown tornado
cases.primary_angle: Investigate how heavy rain limited visibility and why the Waco catastrophe helped spur advances in tornado warnings.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast the historic city damage footprint and 1953 warning process using original mapped records.
cases.verified_core_fact: An F5 tornado devastated central Waco on May 11, 1953; NWS reports 114 deaths and 597 injuries attributable to this tornado.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS city map and Waco city historic aerial/street map; NWS page's Tribune-Herald photographs are explicitly copyrighted.
cases.research_note: City history cites NOAA as a source, so it is not fully independent factual corroboration; archival photos on NWS page credit Waco Tribune-Herald, do not reuse absent permission.

cases.title: The weather window behind the D-Day invasion
cases.primary_angle: Compare competing wartime forecast methods and explain why 6 June was judged marginally workable.
cases.alternate_angle: Show authenticated Allied versus German synoptic charts, noting unequal observational access and analysis times.
cases.verified_core_fact: The invasion of Normandy began June 6, 1944 after forecast conditions prompted postponement from June 5; the Met Office identifies a marginal but usable weather window.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Met Office National Meteorological Archive originals; Met Office source material cites Crown Copyright/Open Government Licence; German DWD charts require separate permission.
cases.research_note: The invasion itself is historical context; meteorological story is forecast uncertainty and narrow weather window. Do not assume German charts are covered by the Met Office OGL.

cases.title: Pine Lake campground tornado in Alberta
cases.primary_angle: A Canadian severe-weather anniversary: show the preconvective enhanced-V satellite signature and real local storm progression.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain why satellite observation times fall on July 15 UTC while the tornado occurred July 14 MDT.
cases.verified_core_fact: A destructive tornado struck Pine Lake, Alberta on July 14, 2000 local time; Public Safety Canada records 12 fatalities.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Authentic NOAA GOES-8/10 and NOAA-12 observations published by UW–Madison CIMSS; determine rights for the particular image, not the satellite platform.
cases.research_note: Canadian disaster database says >140 injured, CIMSS >100; do not quote precise injuries without reconciliation. CIMSS local date July 14 / UTC July 15.

cases.title: Ellicott City's devastating 2016 flash flood
cases.primary_angle: Explain how nearly stationary heavy-rain cells and narrow urban drainage produced rapid flooding.
cases.alternate_angle: Build a real-time warning–rainfall–flooding timeline from the NWS case study and gauge-based USGS research.
cases.verified_core_fact: An intense rainfall episode caused severe flash flooding in historic Ellicott City on July 30, 2016; NWS reports two fatalities.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS local rain gauge and MRMS estimation, USGS hydrology; distinguish estimates, gauges and source copyright.
cases.research_note: This is an upgrade of an existing NCEI Ellicott City lead, not a different occurrence. Do not confuse with the May 27, 2018 flood; keep previous event ID as linked source segment.

cases.title: Hurricane Katrina makes its northern Gulf Coast landfalls
cases.primary_angle: Focus on the distinction between landfall-category winds, the expansive wind field and storm-surge footprint.
cases.alternate_angle: Create a sourced track-and-surge graphic separating Louisiana and Mississippi coastline impacts.
cases.verified_core_fact: Katrina made landfall along the northern Gulf Coast on August 29, 2005, bringing widespread wind and devastating storm surge.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NHC HURDAT2 best track and official TCR; NWS Mobile observed surge data; request individual original photographs if desired.
cases.research_note: NHC and NWS both NOAA: corroborating documents but not institutionally independent. Avoid conflating peak Category 5 Gulf intensity with Category 3 at landfall; distinguish landfalls.

cases.title: The Great Miami Hurricane of 1926
cases.primary_angle: Follow the 35-minute eye lull and how people mistook temporary calm for the end of the storm.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare original Weather Bureau observer notes with modern timing and forecast methods without invented wind readings.
cases.verified_core_fact: The Great Miami Hurricane struck South Florida early September 18, 1926, when short-lead warnings and unfamiliarity with hurricanes worsened its impacts.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: 1926 U.S. Weather Bureau original record and Florida Memory archival collections; photo-specific rights unreviewed.
cases.research_note: Both core sources are within NOAA. Beware differing quoted mortality totals (Miami-area vs full hurricane), later reconstruction of winds and modernized landfall location.

cases.title: The 1927 St. Louis tornado through the city center
cases.primary_angle: Follow the tornado's route through a dense city using period street addresses and photos.
cases.alternate_angle: Explain how contemporary sources differ on casualty totals and how early observational limitations affect estimated intensity.
cases.verified_core_fact: A violent tornado struck central St. Louis on September 29, 1927, leaving extensive damage documented by period photography.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: St. Louis Public Library tornado photo collection and historic street maps; each photo rights status must be checked.
cases.research_note: NWS St. Louis lists 72 deaths, St. Louis Public Library 78, Missouri emergency management 79. Do not publish exact casualty figure before reconciliation. Pre-1970 Fujita ratings are retrospective, not original EF ratings.

cases.title: The Pacific Northwest Columbus Day windstorm
cases.primary_angle: Trace how a powerful extratropical storm generated destructive winds well inland and across the region.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare authentic historic wind observations and the cyclone track without conflating 12–13 October local dates.
cases.verified_core_fact: A historically significant windstorm struck the Pacific Northwest on October 12, 1962.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NOAA archived surface maps, state observatory wind records and documented historical maps; asset rights pending.
cases.research_note: NWS Aberdeen page reproduces externally sourced weather-history graphics, do not assume its images are public domain; check location of peak readings.

cases.title: The record-deep Upper Midwest cyclone of 2010
cases.primary_angle: Explore how a rapidly deepening inland cyclone produced strong winds, tornadoes, blizzard conditions and extreme pressure observations.
cases.alternate_angle: Show Bigfork's measured/derived pressure time series against historically documented inland minima.
cases.verified_core_fact: Bigfork, Minnesota registered a computed sea-level pressure of 955.2 hPa on October 26, 2010 during a powerful extratropical cyclone.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS Duluth source shows station data and pressure graphs; use calculations with station, time and units, not a nationwide record claim.
cases.research_note: NWS explicitly states 955.2 hPa was NOT the lowest pressure ever in CONUS; AWOS sea-level pressure derived from station pressure, and coastal records lower. Avoid misleading all-time US record headlines.

cases.title: The great Florence flood on the Arno River
cases.primary_angle: Tell the meteorological-to-hydrological sequence behind a flood that endangered centuries of cultural heritage.
cases.alternate_angle: Map the Arno flood timeline with authentic high-water marks and documented archival images.
cases.verified_core_fact: After prolonged rain, the Arno overflowed into Florence on November 4, 1966, inundating historic neighborhoods, libraries and artwork.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Italian Civil Protection high-water marker documentation; National Library flood photograph collection and archived records; copyrights unreviewed.
cases.research_note: Italian Civil Protection page lists 35 victims in region; National Central Library says 39. Do not publish a fatality count without scope reconciliation; dated 3–4 Nov overnight.

cases.title: The catastrophic 1977 Andhra Pradesh cyclone
cases.secondary_source_publisher: Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority
cases.primary_angle: Use original Madras cyclone-radar study to show its double-eyewall structure and near-coastal evolution.
cases.alternate_angle: Discuss how observing limitations affected coastal-track and cyclone-intensity interpretation.
cases.verified_core_fact: An intense Bay of Bengal cyclone hit the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 19, 1977, documented by contemporary cyclone-warning radar.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Original IMD radar-study paper charts and state archival cyclone track; article licensing statements conflict and commercial reuse needs checking.
cases.research_note: IMD and Andhra state sources agree broadly on Nov 19 coastal strike, but accounts differ on precise landfall locality (Nizampatnam, Chirala, Bapatla). Do not state exact location, deaths, or max winds as settled.

cases.title: The violent gale and Tay Bridge collapse of 1879
cases.primary_angle: Explain the wind-loading meteorology of the 1879 storm, grounded in contemporary records rather than dramatized artwork.
cases.alternate_angle: Contrast original wind observations, inquiry documents and later wind engineering lessons, carefully separating causes from atmospheric conditions.
cases.verified_core_fact: A violent gale struck Scotland on December 28, 1879, as the Tay Rail Bridge collapsed while a train crossed.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: National Records of Scotland inquiry records, archival bridge plans, historical barometric analyses; individual image rights pending.
cases.research_note: National Records say 59 known passengers/victims versus inquiry estimate ~74–75 aboard; other histories quote ~75. Do not assert the precise death count or wind alone as sole engineering cause.

cases.title: The Burns' Day Storm brings damaging daytime winds to Britain
cases.primary_angle: Show how a rapidly moving extratropical cyclone produced severe daytime gusts across a heavily populated region; explain why timing mattered.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare the Met Office's 12 UTC synoptic analysis and observed gust distribution with the 1987 storm, using consistent wind measures.
cases.verified_core_fact: On 25 January 1990 an intense extratropical depression tracked across southern Scotland and brought severe daytime winds to England and Wales.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Met Office document provides a 12 UTC analysis and station gust chart; verify underlying data availability and reuse terms before redrawing.
cases.research_note: Royal Meteorological Society and Met Office are distinct organizations, but the Society cites Met Office wind data; do not call measurement evidence independent. 47 reported deaths and 93 kt maximum gust are source claims pending claim-level review. Historic chart and photos not asset-cleared.

cases.title: The 2003 Presidents' Day snowstorm reaches the Mid-Atlantic
cases.location: Central Pennsylvania and Washington metropolitan area
cases.primary_angle: Show how the storm spread a wide swath of heavy snow across the Mid-Atlantic, with multi-day snowfall totals clearly dated.
cases.alternate_angle: Compare 16–18 February snowfall gradients and snow-versus-sleet differences in central Pennsylvania and the Washington area.
cases.verified_core_fact: By 16 February 2003 a major snowstorm was affecting central Pennsylvania and the Washington region; snow persisted in parts of the region through 18 February.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: NWS State College maps co-op/spotter totals through 17 February; obtain station-by-station totals and timeframe before original mapping.
cases.research_note: This is a multi-day 16–18 February event, not a one-day snowfall record. The Washington Post article provides contemporary independent reporting for the DC region, not a full-storm independent meteorological analysis. NWS page reports 12–30 inch regional snowfall but any numeric claim needs station and time-window verification. Rights of photographs not checked.

cases.title: The 1965 Palm Sunday tornado outbreak strikes the Great Lakes
cases.location: Indiana and neighboring Great Lakes states
cases.secondary_source_publisher: Wells County Historical Society and Museum
cases.primary_angle: Explain why tornadoes spread across several states and how the warning-to-public communication chain worked in 1965.
cases.alternate_angle: Use a new, sourced tornado-path schematic to describe the unusual near-simultaneous tornadoes without republishing copyrighted news photographs.
cases.verified_core_fact: On 11 April 1965 multiple destructive tornadoes struck Indiana and other Midwestern/Great Lakes states during the Palm Sunday outbreak.
cases.graphic_data_source_note: Use official storm-track data and original geographic rendering; famous Paul Huffman twin-tornado and press photos have distinct copyright ownership and are NOT cleared.
cases.research_note: NWS Indianapolis and Wells County Historical Society support event/date/Indiana impacts. Published outbreak-wide death counts differ between NWS summaries (e.g. 260 vs 271); do not include totals without defining source, time frame and tornado scope. Historic photos are not cleared for reuse. 1965 warning methods must be independently and accurately characterized.

held_candidates.decision: HOLD — do not replace weak primary yet
held_candidates.research_gap: Guinness pages describe the account with January 27 versus January 28 timing; original published historical account and method of measurement need checking. Do not treat 15-inch size as an instrument-measured record or silently assign occurrence day.
